WHY THESE ARE EBITDA-PER-TONNE AND NOT THE TWO PRICES THE SPEC ASKS FOR.
aluminium.yaml models Novelis as can_sheet_spread revenue MINUS a scrap and
primary metal cost. That decomposition has no market data behind it: neither
`can_sheet_spread` nor `al_scrap_midwest` has a free published series, and
neither is on the Daily Metals Pack (all 36 columns checked -- column 8 is
Turkey STEEL scrap and has been dead since 2020-12-03).
What everyone who actually models this company uses is EBITDA per tonne:
Hindalco discloses it every quarter, Novelis discloses it every quarter, and
Kotak forecasts it directly. Three independent parties, one metric. That is
the evidence for re-speccing Novelis on EBITDA/t rather than continuing to
wait for two assessed series that are not coming.
These rows are INPUTS TO A DECISION, not a feed. They do not make Novelis
scoreable from its own spec -- al_scrap_midwest still has no source.
SUPERSEDED 2026-08-25: an earlier version of this note ended 'it stays
peer_group: null, so run_scores skips it by design'. Novelis IS now scored --
a flat 3.0 on every pillar from specs/placeholders.yaml, written by the
placeholder-only second pass in run_scores.py. peer_group is still null (the
schema forbids one on an untradeable unit), so the main loop still skips it;
what changed is that being skipped no longer means being absent.
PERIOD MATTERS. FY26 is a full year ended 2026-03-31 and is depressed by the
Oswego plant fires. 1QFY27 is the quarter ended 2026-06-30, during which the
hot mill restarted -- so it is a recovery quarter, not a clean run-rate. The
two Kotak figures are FORECASTS and are marked as such in `factor`; do not
let an estimate resolve as an observation of fact.

DIRECTION SIGN CONVENTION: the column is impact on NOVELIS/HINDALCO, not the direction of the metric. So 'lower aluminum scrap prices' is +1 -- scrap is a cost, a fall in it helps. Getting this backwards is the exact trap schema.sql:116 warns about.

Adjusted EBITDA of $516 million, up 24% YoY
Rolled product shipments of 916 kilotonnes, down 5% YoY

Adjusted EBITDA increased 24% year-over-year to $516 million in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, driven primarily by lower aluminum scrap prices and cost efficiencies, which were partially offset by higher net tariffs.
Record Novelis quarterly Adjusted EBITDA* at ₹4,875 crore, up 37%
"Adjusted EBITDA at $ Mn" for FY26 was "$1,645"; "Shipments" for FY26 totaled "3,557" KT; "EBITDA/tonne" was "$462" per tonne
Record Aluminium quarterly Upstream EBITDA at ₹7,390 crore, up 81%, driven by favourable macros and stronger operational performance
Consolidated EBITDA for the first quarter stood at ₹14,989 crore, up 73% from the same quarter last year.
EBITDA at a historic high of ₹22,671 crore for the full year
We raise estimates and forecast EBITDA per ton of US$545/577 per ton in FY2027/28E (+9.3%/9% versus earlier).

We expect Novelis’ business to recover strongly from 2HFY27, led by (1) the Oswego plant’s recommencement, which supplies high-margin auto sheets, (2) benefits from higher scrap spreads in the US as volumes are likely to pick up after normalcy at Oswego and (3) the ramp-up of Bay Minette from FY2028E.
